items.heading: Checking and topping up engine oil
precautionsFirst: Check the oil level on level ground, with the engine cold or off for a few minutes.
Avoid overfilling beyond the maximum mark on the dipstick.
details: Open the bonnet and locate the dipstick, usually marked with a bright handle.
Pull it out, wipe it clean with a cloth, reinsert it fully, then pull it out again to check the level against the min/max marks.
If low, add the manufacturer-recommended oil grade a little at a time through the oil filler cap, rechecking the dipstick between additions.
Replace the dipstick and filler cap securely when done.

items.heading: Checking tire pressure and changing a flat tire
precautionsFirst: Park on flat, stable ground away from traffic, engage the handbrake, and use wheel chocks if available before jacking up the car.
Never place any part of your body under a vehicle supported only by a jack.
details: Check tire pressure with a gauge when the tires are cold, comparing it to the recommended PSI on the door frame sticker.
To change a flat, loosen the wheel nuts slightly before jacking the car up.
Jack the car up until the flat tire is clear of the ground, then remove the nuts fully and the wheel.
Fit the spare wheel, hand-tighten the nuts, lower the car, then fully tighten the nuts in a star, or criss-cross, pattern.
Drive cautiously to a service center to have the flat tire repaired and the spare checked.

items.heading: Jump-starting a car battery
precautionsFirst: Never let the positive and negative clamps touch each other or touch metal surfaces incorrectly, as this can cause sparks or damage.
Connect the final ground clamp to an unpainted metal surface away from the battery, not to the dead battery's negative terminal.
details: Park the working vehicle close enough for the cables to reach, with both cars switched off.
Connect the red positive clamp to the dead battery's positive terminal, then the other red clamp to the working battery's positive terminal.
Connect the black negative clamp to the working battery's negative terminal, then the final black clamp to an unpainted metal part of the dead car's engine bay, away from the battery.
Start the working car, let it run a few minutes, then try starting the dead car.
Once started, remove the clamps in reverse order and let the revived car run or drive for a while to recharge the battery.

items.heading: Replacing windshield wiper blades
precautionsFirst: Be careful when the wiper arm is lifted off the windshield, as it can snap back suddenly.
details: Lift the wiper arm away from the windshield until it locks in the raised position.
Locate the small tab or clip connecting the old blade to the arm, and press or slide it to release the blade.
Slide the new blade onto the arm until it clicks securely into place.
Gently lower the wiper arm back onto the windshield and test.

items.heading: Cleaning a two-wheeler air filter
precautionsFirst: Let the engine cool completely before accessing the air filter housing.
details: Remove the air filter housing cover, usually secured with a few screws or clips.
Take out the filter element and tap it gently to remove loose dust, or wash it if it is a washable foam type, following the manual for the correct cleaner and oil.
Let it dry fully before reinserting.
Replace a paper-type filter entirely if heavily clogged or torn, rather than washing it.

items.heading: Lubricating a bike or motorcycle chain
precautionsFirst: Keep hands and loose clothing away from the chain while the wheel is turning.
details: Clean the chain with a rag and a chain-cleaning brush to remove dirt and old grime.
Apply a dedicated chain lubricant along the inner side of the chain while slowly rotating the wheel or pedal.
Let the lubricant penetrate for a few minutes, then wipe off any excess from the outside to avoid attracting dust.
